items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1959-10-26
items.q: The interviewer asks 'Mr. Marocca, did you ever play...?' and the interviewee responds 'No, I didn't.' indicating no personal interaction or relationship beyond the interviewer's query.

ctx.x: And he couldn't make a living in music. He had to do other things besides playing music. Because most of the people that hired you then for a birthday party, something got you for nothing. They got a group of musicians together and that's all. You got food and drink and that's all you got. There was nothing to take home.
Mr. Marocca, did you ever play, or not play, but sing or have anything to do with the St. Alphonsus choir?

No, I didn't. But I did sing at the closing exercise. And there was a man who used to teach us there, was named Sokola. His first name, I can't remember. But he used to put on the show for us. And we were singing the Holy City. Ta-da, ta-da, ta-da, ta-da, Hosanna, and so on. And I used to sing counter melodies against it. At that time I didn't know anything.
